title: Thresholded Wavefront Sentinel for Model Admittance
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a configurable "wavefront sentinel" policy engine that gates model variant admittance into production traffic based on thresholded cohorts and adaptive step schedules. The sentinel combines cohort-level telemetry (latency, error rate, cost-per-token, quality regressed against eval prompts) with a tiny shadow probe sampler and an entropy detector to decide per-step traffic increases, hold conditions, or auto-rollbacks. Goal: provide a single declarative policy surface for canaries, A/B slices, and shadow rollout probes with clear guardrails and observable decision traces.
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL: new 'wavefront' stanza added to rollout API accepting thresholds for latency, p99, error-rate, quality-drop, and cost delta
Shadow probe integration: can configure N% of traffic to shadow probe that variants are validated against without affecting user responses
Adaptive steps: engine autonomously adjusts step durations based on cohort variance and can pause automatically when thresholds are breached
Auto-rollback: if configured thresholds are persistently violated for M consecutive windows, rollback is triggered and recorded
Observability: per-step decision traces emitted to the Console with links to the metric window and the trigger reason
E2E tests: integration test covering normal ramp, transient spike pause, and rollback path using synthetic cohort traffic
decision_log: 2025-02-13 - Design sync: choose cohort hedging approach instead of single global thresholds to avoid noisy population effects
2025-02-14 - Engineering: agreed to implement both hard and soft thresholds; soft thresholds map to advisory holds whereas hard thresholds trigger rollback
2025-02-16 - PM feedback: require a 'grace window' parameter to avoid overreacting to short-lived blips from upstream infra
2025-02-18 - Observability: include a compact decision payload in traces so Console can render 'why' the step advanced or aborted
comments: 2025-02-12 - Ava Martinez: Initial ticket created after postmortem discussion about a canary that progressed too quickly despite cohort divergence.
2025-02-13 - Noah Patel: Prototyped a control loop that samples p95/p99 from cohorts and computes a normalized delta; early results show stable holds on synthetic burst patterns.
2025-02-15 - Priya Singh (QA): Drafted test plan for three scenarios: steady-state ramp, upstream latency spike, and quality regression on a seed prompt set.
2025-02-17 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Noted we should cap shadow probe QPS to avoid affecting billing; suggested default 0.1% traffic for probes and a circuit breaker.

implementation_notes: Wavefront engine will run as a control plane microservice with access to streaming telemetry from the ingest pipeline
Decision windows default to 60s but are configurable per rollout; smaller windows available for low-latency services
Two-tier threshold model: soft_threshold -> pause and alert; hard_threshold -> initiate rollback and cut traffic to baseline variant
Cohorts defined by route + customer segment + region; default fallback to global cohort if granular cohorts lack data
Expose trace id and decision reason on request-level logs for downstream incident analysis
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy metrics cause oscillation. Mitigation: hysteresis + grace window + minimum samples per window
Risk: shadow probes add cost. Mitigation: cap QPS by default and make probe weight billable to non-production ledger
Risk: policy misconfiguration could prevent rollouts. Mitigation: 'dry-run' mode and policy validation that warns on overly strict thresholds
Risk: latency of control loop. Mitigation: use streaming aggregators and local caching of recent windows to keep decision latency < 1s
testing_plan: Unit tests for DSL parser and threshold arithmetic
Integration test with traffic replay harness using cohort split generator
Chaos scenario where backend GPU nodes are killed to ensure hold and rollback behaviors are exercised
Load test to ensure decision engine scales with number of concurrent rollouts (target 2000 active rollouts)
Canary in staging with real-prod telemetry mirrored (shadow) for 48 hours before enabling auto-rollback in prod
